$comment: MCP servers available to the orchestrator. Servers disabled by default are ready to enable once deployed.

servers.name: mcp-notifications
servers.$comment: stdio subprocesses do NOT inherit the container's full env — MCP's StdioServerParameters.env=None merges only a safe allowlist (PATH/HOME/etc, see mcp.client.stdio.get_default_environment), never arbitrary secrets. HA_URL/HA_TOKEN must be listed explicitly here or this server's HA REST calls silently run with an empty token.

servers.name: mcp-filesystem
servers.$comment: Enable once NFS mounts are working and paperless Phase 3 is up

servers.name: mcp-playwright
servers.$comment: Phase 2 — playwright-mcp container must be running

servers.name: mcp-calendar
servers.$comment: CALENDAR_PROVIDER=ha (default) uses HA Google Calendar. This is the canonical calendar path — google-workspace's --tools list deliberately omits 'calendar' to avoid a second, conflicting calendar integration. HA_URL/HA_TOKEN must be listed here explicitly — see mcp-notifications' $comment for why.

servers.name: google-workspace
servers.$comment: Gmail/Docs/Drive via taylorwilsdon/workspace-mcp (PyPI: workspace-mcp). Needs GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET in the container env (set in docker-compose.yml from .env) plus a one-time interactive OAuth consent — see docs/GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_MCP.md. Safe to leave enabled without credentials: discover() catches the failure per-server (registry.py) and the rest of the orchestrator boots normally; it just won't have Gmail/Docs/Drive tools until credentials + consent are done, and self-heals on the next request once they are, no restart needed. Deliberately excludes 'calendar' from --tools — mcp-calendar (HA-backed) is the canonical calendar integration; don't add it here.

servers.name: mcp-shopping-list
servers.$comment: Phase 4 — wraps HA shopping list API

servers.name: mcp-routines
servers.$comment: Phase 4 — stores automation routines in Qdrant
